_analysis_notes.frontend_scope_note: The current frontend is an Angular application for single candidate self-checking against one job description. The required frontend direction is a recruiter-facing screening interface where an employer uploads one job requirement and multiple CVs, then reviews ranked results and summary statistics.
_analysis_notes.current_frontend_note: Frontend already has working Angular routing, a landing page, an analysis page, and a real HttpClient integration with the backend single-file endpoint. However, the UI copy, upload flow, result presentation, and data contract are still candidate-oriented rather than employer-oriented.
important_gaps: The frontend file input accepts PDF, DOC, and DOCX, but the backend currently supports PDF extraction only.
The frontend is wired to a real API for single-file analysis; it is not using a mock store.
The current result view shows one label/message only and does not expose ranked candidate lists or screening statistics.
Project instructions mention Angular 20 guidance, while package.json currently uses Angular 21.1.x.

status_legend.done: Implemented in the frontend and usable as-is
status_legend.partially done: Some frontend implementation exists, but it is incomplete, misaligned with the required flow, or limited to the current single-candidate experience
status_legend.not done: Required frontend capability does not exist yet

features.name: Angular application bootstrap
features.comment: The application is already bootstrapped with standalone Angular components and router configuration.

features.name: Landing page route
features.comment: The root route already renders a landing page and the CTA navigates to the analysis screen.

features.name: Analysis page route
features.comment: A dedicated /analyze route already exists and is connected to the analysis component.

features.name: Recruiter-specific navigation flow
features.comment: Routing exists, but the page flow is still designed around a candidate checking one CV rather than an employer screening many candidates for one job.

features.name: Visual landing screen
features.comment: The landing page is implemented with branding, hero content, imagery, and a working CTA.

features.name: Employer-facing product messaging
features.comment: Current landing copy says 'Find out if a job matches your CV', which targets job seekers instead of recruiters or company owners.

features.name: Recruiter workflow explanation
features.comment: There is no explanation of the new workflow: upload job requirements, upload multiple CVs, review ranked results, and inspect summary analytics.

features.name: Job requirement text input
features.comment: The analysis form already includes a textarea for job description input.

features.name: Single CV upload
features.comment: The form allows selecting a single file and sends it to the backend, but the field labeling implies support for formats the backend does not fully support.

features.name: Multiple CV upload
features.comment: The current file input captures only one file. There is no multiple upload flow or candidate batch preparation UI.

features.name: Structured recruiter fields
features.comment: There are no dedicated fields for job title, department, location, employment type, or optional recruiter metadata.

features.name: Frontend file validation
features.comment: Basic accept filters exist on the input element, but there is no explicit validation for unsupported file types, empty selections, or per-file errors in a batch flow.

features.name: Reactive recruiter form model
features.comment: The screen currently uses template-driven binding for a simple single-candidate form. No recruiter-oriented multi-section or batch-aware form model exists yet.

features.name: Real backend integration
features.comment: The JobFitService uses HttpClient and posts real form-data requests to the backend single-file screening endpoint.

features.name: Single-candidate API contract usage
features.comment: The analysis component is already wired to the current backend response shape and renders a result after a successful request.

features.name: Batch screening API integration
features.comment: No frontend service method or component workflow exists for sending multiple CV files with one job requirement.

features.name: Environment-based API configuration
features.comment: The API base URL is currently hardcoded inside the service instead of being managed through Angular environment configuration.

features.name: Typed recruiter response models
features.comment: The service only models a minimal single-result payload. There are no interfaces for candidate rows, summary cards, ranking metadata, or per-file failures.

features.name: Single result badge display
features.comment: The analysis component already maps the returned label and displays one badge plus a status message.

features.name: Similarity score display
features.comment: The backend returns a score, but the current UI does not display or use it.

features.name: Ranked candidate list
features.comment: There is no table or list for comparing multiple candidates by score and ranking.

features.name: Summary statistics cards
features.comment: The interface does not show totals such as total CVs, shortlisted, under review, rejected, or acceptance percentages.

features.name: Employer-facing report layout
features.comment: There is no dashboard-style result presentation suitable for recruiter review or project submission requirements.

features.name: Export-ready result presentation
features.comment: The frontend has no CSV export, print view, or report-friendly presentation for screening outcomes.

features.name: Loading state during analysis
features.comment: The submit button switches to an analyzing state and becomes disabled during the request.

features.name: Toast-based error feedback
features.comment: The component already shows toast feedback for missing inputs and API failures.

features.name: Reset workflow
features.comment: The Try Again action clears the current single-result state and form values.

features.name: Batch progress and per-file feedback
features.comment: The UI does not support progress reporting, per-file validation messages, or partial failure handling for multi-file screening.

features.name: Empty-state guidance for recruiter results
features.comment: There are no dedicated empty, no-results, or no-match states tailored to employer review.

features.name: Responsive baseline layout
features.comment: Global styles already include responsive adjustments for the landing and analysis screens.

features.name: Component-specific styling structure
features.comment: Feature SCSS files exist, but most actual styling is still centralized in the global styles.scss file.

features.name: Recruiter dashboard visual system
features.comment: The current design is a simple candidate-focused marketing screen, not a recruiter dashboard or screening workspace.

features.name: PrimeNG-based UI layer
features.comment: Project instructions call for PrimeNG usage, but the current UI is built with native HTML elements and custom global CSS.

features.name: Consistent employer terminology across screens
features.comment: Labels, CTAs, helper text, and result messaging are still centered on the candidate point of view.

recommended_frontend_execution_order: Replace candidate-facing copy with recruiter-facing messaging on the landing and analysis screens.
Refactor the analysis screen into a recruiter screening form that accepts one job requirement and multiple CV files.
Update the frontend service layer to call the future batch screening endpoint and model its typed response.
Add a results dashboard with ranked candidate rows, score visibility, and summary statistic cards.
Resolve the upload-format mismatch by either restricting the UI to PDF or coordinating with backend DOCX support.
Move API base configuration out of the service into environment-based configuration and clean up global-vs-component styling boundaries.
